text: 先说一个题外的事情，台湾有一个公益组织，是为残疾人提供服务，这些残疾人，连自己给自己打✈️都无法完成。
en: Let me first mention something off-topic: in Taiwan there is a charity organisation that provides services for people with disabilities, and these people with disabilities cannot even manage to masturbate by themselves.

text: 所以我们要讨论的并不是要不要支持合法，而是在非婚状态下，人是否有性权利，性权利是否要建立在爱的基础上。
en: Therefore, what we ought to discuss is not whether to support legalisation, but rather whether, outside of marriage, people have sexual rights, and whether sexual rights must be founded on a basis of love.

text: 如果有这个权利，那该如何解决。
en: If such a right exists, then how should it be addressed?

text: 任何事情，要先找到最根本的问题，再找对应的解决办法，而不是直接否定一个答案。
en: With any matter, one must first identify the most fundamental problem, and only then find the corresponding solution, rather than simply rejecting an answer outright.

text: 帽子叔叔们，每年明年的都会开展扫黄打非专项行动，然后这个东西每年都屡禁不止。
en: The police conduct special anti-pornography and anti-illegal-publication operations every single year, yet this phenomenon is banned year after year without ever being eradicated.

text: 我认为最主要的原因是社会上有需求，借用成龙大哥的公益一句广告语。
en: I believe the primary reason is that there is demand in society, to borrow a line from a public-service advert by Jackie Chan.

text: 那就是没有买卖就没有伤害。
en: That is: no trade, no harm.

text: 为什么屡禁不止？
en: Why does it persist despite repeated bans?

text: 最主要的原因是这一行赚钱啊！
en: The primary reason is that this line of work makes money!

text: 有句俗话叫，手扶床，脚蹬墙，再疼也比上班强。
en: There is a common saying: hand on the bed, foot against the wall—however much it hurts, it still beats going to work.

text: 大部分的卖淫女在接受过帽子叔叔的教育改造之后被遣返回原籍，过了不久，风声小了，又会重操旧业。
en: Most women in prostitution, after being educated and reformed by the police and then deported to their place of origin, before long, once the fuss dies down, return to their old trade.

text: 为什么不能合法化？
en: Why can it not be legalised?

text: （先别急着喷，此合法化非彼合法化）
en: (Don't be so quick to flame me; this 'legalisation' is not that 'legalisation'.)

text: 国内禁止，以劳务输出的形式在国外合法。
en: Prohibited domestically, yet legal abroad in the form of labour export.

text: 以劳务输出的形式在国外合法化。
en: Legalise it abroad in the form of labour export.

text: 这一点完全可以借鉴小日子过得不错的人的做法。
en: On this point we can absolutely draw lessons from the approach taken by the Japanese.

text: 明治维新后，日本开始了近现代的崛起。
en: After the Meiji Restoration, Japan began its modern rise.

text: 当时的日本要钱没钱、要物没物，还得应付西方列强侵略，所以富国强兵、海外扩张论，就成了头号任务。
en: At that time Japan had no money to speak of and no goods to speak of, and still had to cope with the aggression of Western powers; thus the doctrines of 'enriching the country and strengthening the military' and 'overseas expansion' became the number-one task.

text: 明治政府瞅了一圈，发现他们虽然啥都没有，但色情这一块可是拿捏的死死的。
en: The Meiji government looked around and found that although they had nothing at all, they absolutely had the sex trade locked down.

text: 女人既然可以挣本国人的钱，自然也能挣外国人的钱。
en: Since women could earn money from their own countrymen, naturally they could also earn money from foreigners.

text: 反正都是卖，卖谁不是卖？
en: Anyway it is all selling; who you sell to—isn't it still selling?

text: 于是日本独创了一种新的殖民方式：卖淫殖民！
en: Thus Japan invented a new form of colonisation: prostitution colonialism!

text: 官方出面将大量女青年贩卖到海外，许可并支持她们出国卖春。
en: The authorities stepped in and trafficked large numbers of young women overseas, permitting and supporting them to go abroad to sell sex.

text: 这些背井离乡、卖淫为生的女性，就是赫赫有名的“南洋姐”。
en: These women who left their homes and made a living through prostitution are the renowned 'Nanyang sisters'.

text: 仅在明治年间，日本输出的南洋姐就多达十几万，流动范围从北边直达中国东北部，向南以上海、香港为据点，伺机进入以新加坡为核心的马来半岛，将势力延伸到印度，甚至连非洲都不放过。
en: In the Meiji era alone, the number of Nanyang sisters exported by Japan reached as many as several hundred thousand; their range of movement stretched from the north all the way to north-east China, and to the south, using Shanghai and Hong Kong as bases, they waited for opportunities to enter the Malay Peninsula centred on Singapore, extending their influence as far as India, and not even sparing Africa.

text: 可谓是妓女版的大航海，形成了世界史上罕见的卖淫人口大流动。
en: It can be called a prostitutes' version of the Age of Discovery, forming a great movement of prostitute populations rarely seen in world history.

text: 在急需资本原始积累的明治时期，南洋姐们通过卖身，从海外换取了大量外汇资金，成为日本第五大外汇来源，扩大了日本资本的运作。
en: During the Meiji period, which urgently needed primitive capital accumulation, the Nanyang sisters, through selling their bodies, earned large amounts of foreign exchange from overseas, becoming Japan's fifth-largest source of foreign currency and expanding the operation of Japanese capital.

text: 由于海外南洋姐对本国商品的需求量大，日本大型商社、运输公司、传播公司、银行等大型企业，完成了对海外地区的经济占领，逐渐在世界各地形成了日本人社区。
en: Because the overseas Nanyang sisters demanded large quantities of their home country's goods, Japan's large trading companies, transport firms, media companies, banks and other big enterprises accomplished an economic occupation of overseas regions, and gradually formed Japanese communities all over the world.

text: 也就是在这个基础上，日本才能在各个国家设立领事馆，政府层面的政治军事任务，从此开始展露。
en: It was only on this basis that Japan was able to establish consulates in various countries, and governmental political and military missions began to emerge from then on.

text: 踩着南洋姐身体爬上来的日本，用她们赚来的钱购买船舰，打赢了甲午战争，侵占了我们的辽东半岛、澎湖列岛、台湾岛及所有附属岛屿，迫使大清赔款两亿三千万两白银。
en: Japan, which clawed its way up by trampling on the bodies of the Nanyang sisters, used the money they earned to purchase warships, won the First Sino-Japanese War, occupied our Liaodong Peninsula, the Penghu Islands, Taiwan Island and all their affiliated islands, and forced the Qing dynasty to pay an indemnity of 230 million taels of silver.

text: 百万女子下南洋，卖身买武器，只为侵略他国，日本为何会集体发疯呢？
en: A million women went down to Nanyang, sold their bodies to buy weapons, solely to invade other countries—why did Japan go collectively mad?

text: 日本发动侵华战争真的只是一小撮法西斯分子挑起的吗？
en: Was the war of aggression that Japan launched against China really provoked by only a small handful of fascists?

text: 被军国主义疯狂洗脑的普通老百姓，真的只是战争的受害者吗？
en: Were ordinary people, crazed and brainwashed by militarism, really only victims of the war?

text: 有人曾经算过一笔账，按照当时日本的物价来说，武装一名日本士兵从军装、头盔到步枪、刺刀以及所需的子弹和手榴弹的需要125日元。
en: Someone once did the maths: according to the prices in Japan at the time, arming one Japanese soldier—from his uniform and helmet to his rifle, bayonet, and the required bullets and grenades—cost 125 yen.

text: 而到南洋卖身的女人，一个人一年赚到的钱可以武装起2400名日军。
en: Yet a woman who sold herself in Nanyang could, in a single year, earn enough to arm 2,400 Japanese soldiers.

text: 要是将所有日本女人赚到的外汇加起来，一年足够为日本攒下一艘巡洋舰。
en: If you added up all the foreign exchange earned by Japanese women, in a single year it would be enough for Japan to save up for a cruiser.

text: 在明治维新时期，日本输出的海外妓女总创收可能达1020万日元之多。
en: During the Meiji Restoration period, the total earnings of the overseas prostitutes exported by Japan may have reached as much as 10.2 million yen.

text: 这在当时是什么概念，就这么说吧，根据日本文献记载，明治维新时期的国内采矿业的总投资为800万日元；铁路建设总花费1400万日元；兴建的长崎造船所为62万日元…
en: What did that mean at the time? To put it this way: according to Japanese documents, total investment in the domestic mining industry during the Meiji Restoration period was 8 million yen; total railway construction spending was 14 million yen; and the Nagasaki shipyard that was built cost 620,000 yen…

text: （日本二战著名的战列舰“武藏”号，就在长崎造船厂建造。
en: (The famous Japanese battleship Musashi of the Second World War was built at the Nagasaki shipyard.

text: 另外战列舰雾岛号、航母天成号，以及潜水母舰迅鲸号等大量军舰都在该厂建造。
en: Moreover, the battleship Kirishima, the aircraft carrier Amagi, the submarine tender Jinkyo, and many other warships were built at that yard.

text: 二战后三菱重工建造了日本海上自卫队超过三分之一的舰艇。
en: After the Second World War, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries built more than a third of the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force's vessels.

text: 目前日本海上自卫队最新的爱宕级驱逐舰、秋月级驱逐舰、苍龙级潜艇等大批先进舰艇都是在此建造。
en: At present, the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force's newest Atago-class destroyers, Akizuki-class destroyers, Sōryū-class submarines and many other advanced vessels are all built there.

text: 1902年，日本出口物品换外汇的前五名分别是：
en: In 1902, the top five Japanese exports by foreign-exchange earnings were:
1. Raw silk — 76.86 million yen

text: 2，绢织物——2798万日元
en: 2. Silk fabrics — 27.98 million yen
3. Cotton — 19.90 million yen

text: 4，成品煤炭——1727万日元
en: 4. Finished coal — 17.27 million yen

text: 5，南洋姐的寄回来的外汇——1202万日元。
en: 5. Foreign exchange sent back by the Nanyang sisters — 12.02 million yen.

text: 所以，将这个合法化，我认为是目前扫黄打非行动，最一劳永逸的方法。
en: Therefore, legalising this, in my view, is the most once-and-for-all method for the current anti-pornography and anti-illegal-publication campaigns.

text: 在每年扫黄打非的时候，对于那些多次被抓，被教育被遣返后，又继续从事卖淫活动的女性，完全可以由国家支持成立专门的海外劳务派遣公司，将他们以劳务输出的形式输送到海外去。
en: During the annual anti-pornography and anti-illegal-publication campaigns, for those women who have been caught multiple times, educated and deported, and then go back to prostitution, the state could fully support the establishment of specialised overseas labour-export companies to send them abroad in the form of labour export.

text: 这样子，一方面解决了国内的大量的人口就业，另外一方面，也创造了大量的外汇。
en: In this way, on the one hand it creates a great deal of domestic employment, and on the other hand it also creates a large amount of foreign exchange.

text: 何乐而不为呢？
en: Why not?

text: 我只知道，以前打击组织卖淫不严的那些年，我们城边的河里经常有女性工作者的浮尸
en: All I know is that in those years when the crackdown on organised prostitution was lax, there were often floating corpses of female workers in the river by our city.

text: 我还以为回答和评论会是一边倒的禁止，没想到基本全是明里暗里的支持
en: I had thought the replies and comments would be overwhelmingly in favour of prohibition, but unexpectedly they were basically all supportive, openly or covertly.

text: 我还是第一次见全是和谐删除的评论
en: It is the first time I have seen comments that were all censored and deleted.

text: 很久以前看到过的观点，性越开放的国家，性犯罪率反而越低，而像印度这种连皮肤都要遮住的性压抑国家，女性被强奸的风险反而最大。
en: A viewpoint I saw long ago: the more sexually open a country is, the lower its rate of sexual crime; whereas in sexually repressed countries like India, which even cover up the skin, the risk of women being raped is actually the greatest.

text: 罗翔也说过另一种观点，凭什么短期嫖娼是犯法，长期包养就不是呢？
en: Xiang Luo has also expressed another view: on what basis is short-term soliciting of prostitution illegal, yet long-term keeping of a mistress not?

text: 同样是金钱和性的交易，为什么短期犯法，长期就不犯法？
en: It is the same transaction of money and sex; why is the short-term version against the law, while the long-term version is not?

text: 难道偷一两次东西不犯法，而长期偷东西的人反而不犯法？
en: Is stealing something once or twice not against the law, while a person who steals long-term is instead not against the law?

text: 所以本质上禁止嫖娼不是禁止性和金钱的交易，某些官员比如赖小民包养了上百个情妇，荒谬得很，但是落马之前谁能管的到？
en: So essentially, the prohibition of prostitution is not a prohibition on the transaction of sex and money. Certain officials, such as Xiaomin Lai, kept over a hundred mistresses—utterly absurd—yet before he fell from power, who could have reined him in?

text: 禁止嫖娼只是禁止穷人获得性的满足，真正有钱有权的人有大把渠道用钱去解决性的问题，而法律根本就不会管。
en: Prohibiting prostitution only prohibits the poor from obtaining sexual satisfaction; those who are truly rich and powerful have plenty of channels to use money to resolve their sexual needs, and the law simply does not interfere.

text: 再退一步讲，有的人认为嫖娼会对女性进行剥削和伤害，那为什么要禁止动画色情存在呢？
en: Taking a step back further, some people believe prostitution exploits and harms women, so why then prohibit the existence of animated pornography?

text: 难道这些色情作品也对动画角色产生了性剥削吗？
en: Do these pornographic works also subject the animated characters to sexual exploitation?

text: 所以本质上，所有禁黄，包括极端严厉地打击嫖娼，包括学校刻意制造的性压抑环境，只是在禁止底层人用廉价的方式得到性的满足，有意限制了性的机会，使得这些底层人只能去努力工作，然后凑钱结婚，在婚姻中释放出持续几十年的性压抑，生下更多啥事都不给做，只能劳动的小奴隶。
en: So essentially, all pornography bans—including the extremely harsh crackdown on prostitution, including the sexually repressive environment deliberately created by schools—merely prohibit bottom-rung people from obtaining sexual satisfaction in cheap ways, deliberately restricting sexual opportunity, so that these bottom-rung people can only work hard, then scrape together money to marry, release decades of accumulated sexual repression within marriage, and give birth to even more little slaves who are given nothing to do but labour.

text: 这样，这些奴隶主才能源源不断地得到奴隶的供养。
en: In this way, these slave owners can continuously receive the sustenance of their slaves.

text: 很多被限制的人反而支持这个剥削他的制度，一个国家的意识形态，是其统治阶级所塑造的产物，一个国家的意识形态是服务于这个国家的统治阶级的，鲁迅在《聪明人、傻子和奴才》一文中反讽过这个现象，奴才明明被主人剥削，勇敢的傻子想帮他开一扇窗，他却和其他奴才一起赶跑了那个帮他反抗剥削的人，并且为自己赢得了主人的表扬而沾沾自喜。
en: Many of those who are restricted instead support the system that exploits them. A country's ideology is the product shaped by its ruling class; a country's ideology serves its ruling class. Xun Lu, in his essay 'The Wise Man, the Fool and the Slave', satirised this phenomenon: the slave is clearly exploited by his master, and when the brave fool wants to help him open a window, he joins the other slaves in driving away the person who helped him resist exploitation, and smugly prides himself on having earned his master's praise.

text: 这一点在我写作的《意识形态及政体演进》的第三章里有着重点的描述，描述马克思等人对社会形式和意识形态的阐述，我会将这本书的章节陆续上川到知乎专栏，感兴趣的可以关注我，去看我的专栏。
en: This point is described in detail in Chapter Three of 'Ideology and the Evolution of Political Systems', which I am writing—describing the expositions by Marx and others on social forms and ideology. I will successively upload the chapters of this book to my Zhihu column; those interested may follow me and read my column.
